item.name: Transaction Service

request.description: Milestone 16: this same endpoint now also writes an outbox_events row (aggregate_type='Transaction', aggregate_id=this response's own id, event_type='TransactionCreatedEvent') in the identical local database transaction as the Transaction row returned here — the Transactional Outbox pattern, so the two either both commit or neither does. This response has no outbox_events field (Milestone 16 adds no REST endpoint for that table on purpose, see OutboxEvent's own Javadoc), so a 201 here only confirms the Transaction half. See README.md's "Validating Milestone 16" section, step 3, for the plain-language steps to look at the outbox_events row itself.
All query params are optional and independently combinable — built on JPA Specifications (TransactionSpecifications). Delete any param you don't need.

item.name: Milestone 17 - Test Plan
item.description: Run the folders in order. Every request goes through the API Gateway ({{apiGatewayUrl}}), as a real client would. Each request's Tests tab asserts the expected status and body; the Test Results tab shows pass/fail. Folders 4 and 6 are meant to be run with the Collection Runner (right-click the folder > Run folder, Iterations 60, Delay 0) so the burst arrives faster than the 10 tokens/s refill. Steps that need a container stopped or started say so in their description; those are the only terminal steps.

item.name: 0. Setup
item.description: Creates two users and a category. Run once per session.

request.description: Fresh email per run (timestamp), so this never collides with an earlier run.
Second identity, used to prove rate-limit buckets are per user (folder 5).
user-service profile; its id is the userId every transaction needs.
Category for the transactions below.

item.name: 1. Outbox to Kafka
item.description: The Milestone 17 path: the outbox row written by 1.1 is published to transaction-events by OutboxPublisher within about a second. Verify the Kafka side in Kafka UI (http://localhost:8090 > Topics > transaction-events > Messages): one message whose Key is {{transactionId}}, with headers eventType=TransactionCreatedEvent, aggregateType=Transaction, outboxEventId, X-Correlation-ID={{correlationId}} and traceparent. Topics > transaction-events > Overview shows 3 partitions, replication factor 3.

request.description: Sends an explicit X-Correlation-ID so the resulting Kafka record can be found by it. Expect 201; the record should be on the topic within ~1-2 s.
The business row is readable through the normal REST path.

item.name: 2. Kafka outage - writes keep working
item.description: Before 2.1: stop all three brokers (terminal: docker compose stop kafka-1 kafka-2 kafka-3). 2.1 must still return 201: the event waits in outbox_events with processed_at = NULL, and transaction-service logs 'Outbox event ... not acknowledged, will retry next poll' every few seconds ('Kafka cluster unreachable' instead, if the topic had not been provisioned yet). Then start the brokers again (docker compose start kafka-1 kafka-2 kafka-3); within ~30 s the message for {{transactionId}} appears in Kafka UI and processed_at is set. Variant: stop only kafka-3 — 2.1 is still published immediately (2 of 3 replicas satisfy min.insync.replicas=2).

item.name: 2.1 Create transaction while Kafka is down

request.description: Expect 201 even with every broker stopped.

exec: pm.test('201 Created with Kafka down', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: 3. gRPC deadline and 503 mapping (fix 1)
item.description: 3.1 with everything up. 3.2 after docker compose stop budget-service (UNAVAILABLE). 3.3 after docker compose start budget-service, wait for it to be healthy and ~30 s more (analytics-service re-resolves budget-service's new container address), then docker compose pause budget-service (the process is frozen, so the call can only end by deadline: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED). Finish with docker compose unpause budget-service. 3.1 also proves the analytics-service Gateway route added in this milestone.

request.description: Expect 200 with the summary (empty items is fine: no budgets created).
Expect 503 ProblemDetail quickly (connection refused / name not resolvable).
Expect 503 after about 2 s: the deadline, not an indefinite hang.

exec: pm.test('ends at the deadline (~2s), not later', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.above(1500); pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(4000); });

item.name: 4. Rate limit - user A burst (Runner: 60 iterations, delay 0)
item.description: Bucket key is user:<user A's JWT subject>. Burst capacity 20, refill 10/s: expect roughly the first 20-30 iterations 200 and the rest 429 (the split varies with how fast your machine sends; the last iteration asserts at least one 429 occurred). Every 429 is checked for the RFC 7807 body and Retry-After (fix 5). The Runner sends one request at a time, so a 429 needs the average round trip under ~100 ms; if the last iteration's check fails on a slow machine, re-run with 100 iterations. Run folder 5 immediately after.

request.description: 200 until user A's bucket is empty, then 429.

exec: pm.test('burst produced at least one 429 across the run', () => pm.expect(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('count429'))).to.be.above(0));

item.name: 5. Rate limit - user B unaffected
item.description: Run right after folder 4 while user A is still throttled. Same client IP, different user: must be 200, which proves buckets are keyed by principal, not IP (fix 3).

request.description: Expect 200: user B has a full bucket of its own.

item.name: 6. Rate limit - anonymous by X-Forwarded-For (Runner: 60 iterations, delay 0)
item.description: No token, so the key falls back to the client IP from X-Forwarded-For (ip:203.0.113.10). Expect 429s after the burst. Then edit the header to 203.0.113.20 and send once: 200 again, a different bucket. That second result is also the caveat: with nothing in front of the Gateway, a client controls this header — see spendwise.rate-limit.trusted-proxy-hops in config-repo/api-gateway.yml.

request.description: Empty JSON body: auth-service rejects it with 400 at validation, before any password hashing, so the burst outpaces the refill. 400 while allowed; 429 once the IP bucket is empty.

exec: pm.test('400 while allowed, 429 when throttled', () => pm.expect([400, 429]).to.include(code));
pm.test('burst produced at least one 429 across the run', () => pm.expect(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('count429'))).to.be.above(0));

item.name: 7. Redis down - fail fast (fix 4)
item.description: Before 7.1: docker compose stop redis. Rate limiting fails open (requests allowed) and must not add latency. Afterwards: docker compose start redis.

request.description: Expect 200 well under a second; X-RateLimit-Remaining is -1, RedisRateLimiter's fail-open marker.
